lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Data: Scaled Graphs and Measurement Line Plots
lessonRef.focus: judging whether a real graph is honest
lessonRef.title: Transfer, reflection, and publication: judging whether a real graph is honest

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different setting than the problems below.

items.prompt: A scaled bar graph uses a scale of 5 per symbol. A bar shows 3 symbols. What does that bar represent?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: On a scaled bar graph with 2 per symbol, "Red" has 4 symbols and "Blue" has 2 symbols. How many more does "Red" have than "Blue"?
A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 5 per symbol. The bar for "Fish" is worth 4 symbols. How many does "Fish" represent?
On a scaled bar graph with 5 per symbol, "Apples" has 8 symbols and "Bananas" has 6 symbols. How many more does "Apples" have than "Bananas"?
A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 5 per symbol. The bar for "Cats" is worth 1 symbols. How many does "Cats" represent?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: On a scaled bar graph with 5 per symbol, "Red" has 4 symbols and "Blue" has 1 symbols. How many more does "Red" have than "Blue"?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 5 per symbol. The bar for "Cats" is worth 5 symbols. How many does "Cats" represent?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
